quotes.text: a good threshold to measure is the 75th percentile of page loads, segmented across mobile and desktop devices.
Tools that assess Core Web Vitals compliance should consider a page passing if it meets the recommended targets at the 75th percentile for all three
Stable Core Web Vitals metrics won't change more than once per year.
While lab measurement is an essential part of delivering great experiences, it is not a substitute for field measurement.
if at least 75 percent of page views to a site meet the "good" threshold, the site is classified as having "good" performance
the Core Web Vitals recommended thresholds are not segregated by device and the same threshold is used for both.
we conclude a 200 ms is a reasonable "good" threshold for most sites, and greater than 500 ms is a reasonable "poor" threshold.
A page must be publicly discoverable to be considered for inclusion in the CrUX dataset.
The page is served with an HTTP status code other than 200 (after redirects).
eligible user experiences on all of that origin's pages are aggregated at the origin-level, regardless of individual page discoverability.
Origins or pages having more than 20% of their total traffic excluded due to ineligible combinations of dimensions are excluded entirely from the dataset.
These identifiers are stripped from the URL in the CrUX dataset so that all user experiences on the page are aggregated together.
The data in the Chrome UX Report is a 28-day rolling average of aggregated metrics.
Using the CrUX API requires a Google Cloud API key provisioned for Chrome UX Report API usage.
The CrUX API is limited to 150 queries per minute per Google Cloud project, which is offered without charge.
Complex actions like following redirects are not handled.
